speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the shooting pain in your ear and when it started after your tympanoplasty? Also, does the pain worsen when you try to wear earrings or touch the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any jaw clicking, locking, or pain in the temporomandibular joint when you open your mouth wide? I want to rule out temporomandibular joint disorder, which can cause referred ear pain and is often exacerbated by stress.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any visible signs of infection, such as redness or swelling, in the earlobe piercing site or deep within the ear canal? I need to determine if this is a localized inflammatory issue like perichondritis or chondritis versus a deeper surgical complication.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate to your jaw or teeth, and do you notice any clicking or popping sounds in your jaw joint when you chew? I suspect temporomandibular joint disorder may be causing referred pain to the ear.
